# Get started on FreeRTOS POSIX

<!-- type: how-to · level: 1 -->

**Needs first:** [Install](../start/install.md)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by scripts/gen-board-support.py: starter status -->
> **Status:** Verified on host (daily). From the board support registry: [`nros-board-freertos-posix`](../reference/boards/freertos-posix.md); [Board Support Levels](../reference/board-support-levels.md) explains the words.
<!-- END GENERATED starter status -->

This starter puts a talker on the FreeRTOS kernel running as an ordinary
program on your Linux machine, and shows its messages arriving in ROS 2.
FreeRTOS's POSIX port runs the kernel's tasks as threads of one host process,
and the talker uses your host's own sockets, so there is no emulator and no
network to set up. It is the quickest way to see a FreeRTOS application talk
to ROS 2.
You write the talker in Rust, C or C++; pick a tab and every tab on the page follows.

The talker uses Cyclone DDS, which runs inside the talker's own process and
finds its peers on the network the way any ROS 2 node does, so there is no
router to start. The board runs zenoh too, through a router on this machine:
[Zenoh on this board](#zenoh-on-this-board) shows how.

## What you need

- A Linux host with the [install](../start/install.md) done, so `nros` is on
  your `PATH`, and the C toolchain and CMake the install's host packages
  bring.
- ROS 2 (Humble on Ubuntu 22.04, Jazzy on 24.04;
  [which edition](../start/install.md#install-ros-2-first)), with its Cyclone
  DDS middleware, so that `ros2 topic echo` can read what the talker
  publishes. The build also generates the talker's message code from ROS 2's
  message definitions. On Debian or Ubuntu:

```bash probe=30
sudo apt-get install -y ros-humble-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp
```

Nothing else: no board, no cable, and nothing to keep running beside the
talker.

## Provision

```bash probe=32
nros setup freertos-posix --rmw cyclonedds
```

That fetches the FreeRTOS kernel sources, with its POSIX port, and what
Cyclone DDS needs, into a shared store under `~/.nros`. Nothing is installed
system-wide. There is no cross-compiler to fetch: the simulator builds with
your host's compilers.

## Scaffold the project

Source ROS 2 first, in the shell you scaffold from. `nros new` writes
the ROS 2 edition the project speaks, and it takes it from the sourced
ROS 2; with none sourced, it writes Humble. On Jazzy, source
`/opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash` instead:

```bash probe=38
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
```

<!-- tabs -->

### Rust

```bash probe=40
nros new fp_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang rust --rmw cyclonedds
cd fp_ws
```

### C

```bash probe=40
nros new fp_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang c --rmw cyclonedds
cd fp_ws
```

### C++

```bash probe=40
nros new fp_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang cpp --rmw cyclonedds
cd fp_ws
```

<!-- /tabs -->

That wrote a workspace with two packages:

```text
fp_ws/
└── src/
    ├── fp_node/                 # the talker: package.xml, Cargo.toml or CMakeLists.txt, its source
    └── fp_node_bringup/         # package.xml, system.toml, system.contract.yaml: the board, the RMW, the node
```

`fp_node` is the talker, a library with no `main()` that names no board. It
publishes `std_msgs/String` on `/chatter` once a second. `fp_node_bringup`
says what the talker runs on: its `system.toml` holds one image,
`[image.freertos]`, with `board = "freertos-posix"`, and names Cyclone DDS as
the RMW. The FreeRTOS startup task that runs your node is generated from it
when you build.

## Run it on this machine

Build and run from the same shell, where ROS 2 is sourced. This first run
records the ROS 2 prefix in the workspace, so later runs of it need no
sourced shell:

```bash probe=50
nros run fp_node --expect "Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'" --timeout 600
```

`nros run` builds the talker with CMake (the first build compiles the
FreeRTOS kernel, Cyclone DDS and nano-ros, a few minutes; later builds take
seconds) and runs it. With `--expect` it stops the talker and exits 0 at the
first line containing that text, and exits 1 if the talker stops first or
`--timeout` runs out. It prints lines like:

```text
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

Without `--expect` it keeps running until you press Ctrl-C. Start it that way
in one terminal:

```bash probe=60 probe-run=120 probe-keep
nros run fp_node
```

```text probe-expect=60
Publishing: 'Hello World: 2'
```

## See it in ROS 2

Leave `nros run` going. In a second terminal, ask ROS 2 for the topic over
Cyclone DDS:

```bash probe=70 probe-run=90
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=70
data: 'Hello World:
```

Both sides use domain 0, the ROS 2 default, so they find each other with no
configuration. Asking for best-effort receives from a best-effort or a
reliable publisher alike.

## Zenoh on this board

To talk over zenoh instead, the talker dials a zenoh router on this machine,
at `tcp/127.0.0.1:7447`. Install ROS 2's zenoh middleware, which brings the
router, and provision the board for zenoh:

```bash probe=80 variant=zenoh
sudo apt-get install -y ros-humble-rmw-zenoh-cpp
nros setup freertos-posix
```

Scaffold a second workspace beside the first, this time naming zenoh:

<!-- tabs -->

### Rust

```bash probe=82 variant=zenoh
cd ..
nros new fpz_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang rust --rmw zenoh
cd fpz_ws
```

### C

```bash probe=82 variant=zenoh
cd ..
nros new fpz_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang c --rmw zenoh
cd fpz_ws
```

### C++

```bash probe=82 variant=zenoh
cd ..
nros new fpz_ws --board freertos-posix --template talker --lang cpp --rmw zenoh
cd fpz_ws
```

<!-- /tabs -->

Start the router in its own terminal:

```bash probe=84 probe-run=60 probe-keep variant=zenoh
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
```

```text probe-expect=84 variant=zenoh
Started Zenoh router with id
```

Then, back in the workspace, build and run the talker:

```bash probe=86 probe-run=900 variant=zenoh
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run fpz_node --expect "Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'" --timeout 600
```

```text probe-expect=86 variant=zenoh
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

Start it again without `--expect` and leave it going. In another terminal,
`ros2` reads it through the same router, with `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` set to
`rmw_zenoh_cpp`:

```bash probe=88 probe-run=120 probe-keep variant=zenoh
nros run fpz_node
```

```text probe-expect=88 variant=zenoh
Publishing: 'Hello World: 2'
```

```bash probe=89 probe-run=90 variant=zenoh
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=89 variant=zenoh
data: 'Hello World:
```

## If it doesn't work

- **`nros run` stops at once and names `AMENT_PREFIX_PATH`:** this shell has
  not sourced ROS 2, and no earlier build of the workspace recorded it.
  Source it and run again.
- **The zenoh talker prints no `Publishing:` line:** it waits for the
  router. Check that `rmw_zenohd` is running and printed its
  `Started Zenoh router` line.
- **`ros2 topic echo` prints nothing:** check the `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` line,
  and that neither shell sets a `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` other than 0. A firewall that
  drops multicast also stops DDS discovery.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshooting - First 10 Minutes](../reference/troubleshooting-index.md).
